bib.title: What is Missing from AI Post-Training AI: An Empirical Analysis

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "What Is Missing From AI Post-Training AI: An Empirical Analysis". First author Joy Jia Yin Lim (Tsinghua; co-authors Huang, Peng, Lu, Cong, Zhang, Sun, Lin). Preprint, arXiv:2608.19072v2 [cs.AI], 28 Sep 2026 (v1 month not printed; year 2026; the id matches your expectation). No venue ("Preprint").
COVERAGE: 25 of 25 pages read, 91,587 chars, including Appendices A-E and Tables 3-11. References were skimmed. Figures were not rendered. Tables and captions were read from the text extraction.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Agents lock into a default strategy that follows the agent, not the task, and rarely switch.
 number: 74 of 3,557 adjacent training pairs (2.1%) change strategy. Claude Code defaults to full SFT 71.9% of the time, Codex CLI to PEFT 89.5%.
 setup: 1,338 PostTrainBench trajectories (Rank et al. 2026). 7 benchmarks, 4 base models, 3 harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode), 10 h on one H100. 5,111 verified training experiments. Initial strategy recognised in only 814 trajectories. Annotation was rule-based scripts plus an LLM, reviewed by the authors.
 quote: "only 74 of 3,557 adjacent training pairs (2.1%) ever change strategy" (p.2). Table 1 gives per-agent switch rates of 4.5% for Claude Code (54/1,203), 1.6% for Codex CLI (15/943) and 0.4% for OpenCode (5/1,411) (p.4).
 where: p.2 and p.4. The strategy changes split as 35 algorithm, 38 data-source and 1 training-stage (Table 5, p.16).
2. Experience improves execution but not strategy.
 number: gap to the instruct model closed 75.1% against 48.6% for the autonomous baseline. The agent adopted 22 of 22 execution suggestions and 0 of 21 strategy suggestions.
 setup: Qwen3-1.7B-Base. GSM8K, HumanEval and AIME 2025 (AIME scored pass@8). Claude Code with Opus 4.6. 3 runs each, 10 h on 4 A800s. Experience = experiment journal + skill library + evaluator agent.
 quote: "closing 75.1% of the gap to the official instruct model versus 48.6% for the same agent running autonomously" (p.5). "adopts all 22 execution-level suggestions ... but none of the 21 strategy-level ones" (p.6).
 where: Table 2 (p.6), Fig 4, Table 7 (p.19).
3. A single mid-run human instruction to switch beats the agent's own continuation. A bare "reconsider" prompt does not.
 number: +17.44 pp on GSM8K (47.76 to 65.20, SFT to GRPO). HumanEval 52.0 to 62.8 (RFT then GRPO with unit-test reward). AIME pass@8 0/30 to 2/30.
 setup: One forked trajectory per benchmark, same remaining budget. Branch point and alternative were chosen by the authors after the fact. Reconsider forks stayed on SFT and scored GSM8K 48.0, HumanEval 31.7, AIME 1/30.
 quote: "in every such fork, the agent reaffirms its current strategy" (p.8).
 where: Fig 6b (p.8), App D.2, Table 8 (p.22).
4. Human review before training changes which strategy the agent locks into, not whether it locks in. Reasoning compute only refines the committed strategy.
 number: AIME with RL redirect: best 3/30 against baseline 1/30 and experience-driven 2/30 (Fig 6a). On AIME, about 14M extra tokens buy one extra problem. On GSM8K, about 90% of the gain comes in the first half of the token budget, and the remaining ~11M tokens add +2.1 points. HumanEval gets +51.8 points in the first half and +9.8 after.
 setup: As claim 2. The experience-driven agent used 1.8-9.2x more tokens than the baseline.
 where: pp.6-8.
5. Ablations (Table 2, mean of 3 runs on Qwen3-1.7B-Base; average score and gap closed).
 Base 5.44. Official instruct 62.83 (GSM8K 88.70, HumanEval 66.46, AIME 33.33).
 Autonomous baselines: Opus 4.6 33.34 (48.6%), GLM-5.2 32.45 (47.1%), GPT-5.2 on Codex CLI 18.95 (23.5%).
 Experience-driven: 48.55 (75.1%).
 Removing the evaluator agent hurts most: 38.04 (56.8%). Removing the skill library gives 43.64 (66.6%). Removing the journal gives 43.05 (65.5%).
 Full row: GSM8K 77.30±3.8, HumanEval 62.80±6.1, AIME 5.56±1.6.
 quote: "w/o evaluator agent 68.20±6.0 (−9.1)42.60±8.2 (−20.2)3.33±0.0 (−2.2)38.04 56.8%" (p.6).
6. Supporting detail.
 - Execution is reliable: 3.82 training runs and 13.80 evaluations per trajectory on average.
 - Strategy follows agent in every benchmark x base-model cell (Table 4).
 - Audit of 16 trajectories with algorithm changes: 15 of 35 transitions return to SFT, and the effect is mixed (Table 6). One SFT to DPO change regressed (0.539 to 0.478).
 - HumanEval: the evaluator recommended RL in 11 of 14 cycles. The agent wrote GRPO scripts but ran 14 SFT variants and no RL.
 - The agent consulted skills 18-60 times per run but created no new skills.
 - Cross-agent replication (App E): 56 of 64 successful Codex runs used PEFT. GLM-5.2 never changed algorithm. One AIME fix was execution-level: removing a 2,048-token generation cap raised 1/30 and 2/30 to 7/30.
 - Fable 5 runs showed contamination and reward hacking, including edits to the official evaluation interface (App E.3).

LIMITS (authors and observed)
- Controlled experiments use one base model (Qwen3-1.7B-Base), 3 benchmarks, 3 runs per condition, and 10 h on 4 A800s.
- Mid-run forks use one randomly picked trajectory per benchmark. The authors chose the branch point and the alternative. This shows a better route was reachable, not which is best.
- AIME has only 30 problems (1 problem = 3.33 pp). The AIME gains are small-sample, within noise.
- Opus 4.6 was used because newer models (Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Fable 5) were noisier or contaminated.
- The initial strategy is labelled for only 814 of 1,338 trajectories. 733 of 5,111 experiments have no algorithm label.
- Fork training signal is proposed, not tested. No RL or training was done to teach switching.
- The paper's own "no PostTrainBench time-to-lock" caveat: "beginning of a run" means the planning phase.
- The paper is mostly an observational and case-study design, so it is not a controlled causal test of "decision" as the missing factor.

BUILDS ON: PostTrainBench (Rank et al. 2026); Abbasi 2026 (blog on lack of experience); AgentRx (Barke et al. 2026) for trajectory diagnosis; the Lu et al. 2026a RSI framing; Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023), ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024) and Voyager-style skills (Wang et al. 2023) for the experience stack; DAPO (Yu et al. 2025) for the guided GRPO.

BEARS ON / PLACEMENT
- Closest to 05 (post-training for agents). It touches the agent-as-post-trainer side, not post-training methods themselves.
- Weak fit with 07 reward design, 08 reasoning RL, 12 RLHF failure modes. Two minor hooks: the GRPO guided branches use verifiable rewards, and Table 6 / Fig 9 show reward hacking and a metric-mismatch counterexample (DPO).
- Better home is ai-engineering/04-loop-engineering. The finding is about agent loops: execution loops close while strategy loops stay open, explicit continue-or-switch decision nodes, and journal/skill/evaluator scaffolds that do not trigger revisions. It is worth cross-citing from 05 as a one-line pointer.

CODE: none.

FIGURES (not rendered; from captions in text)
- Fig 1 (p.2): timeline of GSM8K runs showing local tuning in a locked strategy. Fastest summary of the thesis.
- Fig 4 (p.6): adopted vs declined suggestions per cycle (22/22 vs 0/21).
- Fig 6 (p.8): guided versus own continuation.
- Fig 7 (p.9): assumed globally closed loop versus observed locally iterative one.
- Fig 9 (p.19): annotated AIME trajectory with no strategy switch.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Extraction was clean, apart from some run-together words in the title and headings and garbled plot axis labels. The auto-mode classifier failed once on a Bash call. I retried by reading the saved extraction (/tmp/lim.txt) instead. Reference text includes future-dated arXiv ids and model names (Opus 5, Fable 5, GPT-5.2). I report them as printed and did not check them.

Verbatim quotes with pages
(a) p.1 abstract: "only 2.1% of transitions between adjacent training runs ever change strategy ... a single mid-run instruction outperforms the agent's own continuation by up to 17.44 points under the same budget."
(b) p.7: "human guidance at the initial decision actually changes which strategy the agent locks into, but not whether it locks in."
(c) p.9: "(1) an interaction protocol that makes "continue or switch" an explicit decision node after each evaluation and before any further action, rather than an implicit option buried in a long context"
